name: Saint Nicholas of Tolentino
history: An Augustinian friar of the Italian Marche who spent thirty years preaching, hearing confessions and caring for the poor and sick of Tolentino. Known for his gentleness and his long hours of prayer, he prayed especially for the souls in purgatory and is honoured as their patron. In 1446 he became the first Augustinian to be canonised.
life: Nicholas was born around 1245 at Sant’Angelo in Pontano. His parents, childless for years, had made a pilgrimage to the shrine of Saint Nicholas at Bari and named their son after him. As a youth, it is said, he heard an Augustinian friar preach on the words love not the world, and asked to join the order. After his ordination he moved between several friaries before settling at Tolentino around 1275, where he stayed until his death in 1305. The town was divided by the feuds of the age, and he preached peace in the streets, visited the sick and the poor, and spent long hours in the confessional. Tradition tells that a dead friar appeared to him asking for prayers, and that he offered Mass for the departed for a week. Blessed bread, known as Saint Nicholas bread, is still given out in his honour.
prayerTo: Saint Nicholas, faithful friar and friend of the holy souls, you prayed for the dead as if they were your own family. Pray for all who have died with no one to remember them, and teach me to offer my prayers, my Masses and my small sufferings for them, trusting in the mercy of God. Amen.
penance: Have a Mass offered for the holy souls, or pray for the dead whom no one remembers. Share bread with someone today in Nicholas’s honour.
meditation: Nicholas spent long hours in prayer for those who had gone before him. Who among your own dead have you forgotten to pray for?
prayer: Be mindful, O Lord, of our humble prayers in this commemoration of Blessed Nicholas, Your Confessor, so that we, who have no confidence in our own righteousness, may be helped by the merits of those who have been pleasing to You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
